subject.title: fix(gateway): reject invalid session history limit with 400 instead of coercing to 1

question: Should the shipped direct session-history HTTP endpoint change malformed or below-one `limit` requests from HTTP 200 with one message to HTTP 400?
rationale: The new behavior is cleaner and matches the minimum-one contract, but it deliberately removes a released fallback that external dashboard clients may currently observe.

options.title: Adopt Strict Validation
options.body: Confirm malformed limits are unsupported, require live valid-and-invalid HTTP proof, and accept HTTP 400 as the canonical contract.

options.title: Preserve Released Behavior
options.body: Keep the coercion fallback and close or redesign this PR if compatibility with existing clients outweighs stricter caller feedback.

recommendation.title: Adopt Strict Validation
recommendation.body: Confirm malformed limits are unsupported, require live valid-and-invalid HTTP proof, and accept HTTP 400 as the canonical contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the direct endpoint and are the strongest feature-history candidate for confirming its intended request contract.
